summary: Stocks ended a choppy week lower on Friday: the S&P 500 slipped 0.5% to 7,623.68, the Nasdaq 0.2% and the Dow 1.2%, with worries about the cost of financing AI spending lingering after Thursday's sharp Nasdaq drop.
Energy shares closed at a record as Brent crude reached its highest level since late April after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia; higher prices are keeping consumer sentiment near a record low.
A heavy week ahead: the Federal Reserve's rate decision and the first estimate of third-quarter GDP both land on Wednesday, Oct 28, hours before Microsoft and Alphabet report.
A global tech sell-off driven by worries over how AI build-outs are being funded pulled down Nvidia, AMD and Dell along with Asian chip and memory makers.
AI-linked stocks including Nvidia, Oracle and CoreWeave fell after a report on OpenAI's revenue raised questions about returns on AI spending.
Nvidia's investments in and financing of AI cloud providers are drawing scrutiny after so-called neocloud stocks fell sharply.
Reports Wednesday, Oct 28 after the close; consensus EPS is $4.71 against $4.13 a year ago. Microsoft guided to Azure growth of about 45% in constant currency.
Reports Wednesday, Oct 28 after the close; consensus EPS is $2.94. Google Cloud revenue grew 82% last quarter, and capital spending will be in focus.
Third-quarter revenue rose 41% in dollars to about $46.7 billion and net income 69%, with a 66.4% gross margin; fourth-quarter revenue is guided to $52.3–54.3 billion.
Record third-quarter sales of €11.7 billion and net income of €5.0 billion; fourth-quarter sales guided to €14.2–15.2 billion, and ASML says planned 2027–28 supply will not fully meet demand.

Third-quarter copper output was about 830 million pounds; the Grasberg mill is running near two-thirds of pre-incident rates, with near-full capacity targeted by end-2027. Earnings are due Tuesday, Oct 27, before the open.
Reports Wednesday, Oct 28 before the open; analysts expect EPS of $4.03 on $12.3 billion of revenue. The stock bounced about 5% from a six-month low in its latest session.
